title: All-Hands March 2026 - talking points + Q&A (draft)
content:
Purpose: quick draft of talking points for the March all-hands. Rough - please add edits inline or drop comments in Slack thread #all-hands-announce.

Structure:
- Opening (CEO) - high-level momentum
- Product updates (PM lead) - hosted API, Dedicated, Private highlights
- Engineering wins - serving runtime, performance + reliability metrics
- People/time-sensitive items (hiring, org changes, upcoming hiring freeze? TBD)
- Customer stories / logos
- Q&A - prepared answers for likely questions

Notes to self (TODO):
- [ ] Confirm CEO availability for opening (asked Jordan on 2026-03-01)
- [ ] Finalize slides + A/V check with SRE (target 2026-03-08)
- [ ] Sync with product on exact phrasing for Dedicated pricing announcement
- [ ] Add 1-2 customer quotes (Samira to provide by 2026-03-05)

Opening (CEO) - 3 minutes (possible script fragments):
- "Quick note: huge momentum since last quarter - adoption growing across PLG and enterprise segments. Thank you to everyone who shipped the scaling work; our latency and reliability improvements are getting noticed by customers."
- Call out: Series C progress - investment in Private and Dedicated; focus on enterprise readiness.
- Tone: optimistic, concise, celebrate operational work.

Product update (Emily/PM lead) - 6-8 minutes
- Hosted API: usage growth metrics (placeholder) - showed 35% QoQ active developer signups (confirm numbers). New features: streaming upgrades (reduced start-up latency), function/tool-calling stable in GA preview.
- Redwood Dedicated: pilot with 3 customers now in production (anonymized). Major highlight: predictable throughput SLA + burst capacity in private-beta.
- Redwood Private: pushed new VPC installer - simplifies on-prem deployments, KMS integration ready.
- Redwood Optimize: rollout of batching recommendations in console; initial customers seeing 20-30% token cost reduction (need ops to validate).
- Quick demo idea: show console per-route latency breakdown (30s - consider cutting if time).

Engineering wins - 4 minutes
- Serving runtime: recent kernel selection improvements reduced tail latency for long-context by ~25% on bench (internal numbers). Note: still tuning quantization path - more work on 8-bit kernels.
- Observability: token-level tracing landed; now possible to track per-request cost back to route. Shout-out to SRE and runtime teams for rollout.

People / org items (HR / People ops) - 2 minutes
- Hiring: top-of-funnel healthy; interviews ramping for infra and SRE.
- Reminders: open nominations for peer awards (link in Slack).

Customer highlights - 2 minutes
- Short anonymized case study: startup X moved to Redwood Dedicated and reduced inference costs by ~40% - currently in anonymized slide (ask Samira for permission).

Prepared Q&A (anticipated questions + draft answers)
- Q: Are we doing any immediate price changes for hosted API?
  A: No immediate across-the-board price changes. We're testing dedicated pricing packages and will communicate via sales for enterprise customers. Any public pricing changes will go through product + finance review.

- Q: When will Private GA?
  A: Private is in limited release; we are expanding the pilot this quarter. GA timeline depends on a few compliance checkpoints - target H2 2026 but not committing publicly until we hit security milestones.

- Q: What do recent reliability incidents mean for SLAs?
  A: Quick honest answer: incidents highlighted areas in our fallback routing logic. We pushed fixes and added more automated smoke tests. SLA work continues; Dedicated customers have separate commitments.

- Q: Will we open-source more infra components?
  A: We remain pragmatic. We'll open-source components that help the ecosystem and are low risk (examples: small runtime utilities). Core orchestration and control planes will remain proprietary for now.

- Q: Are there layoffs / hiring freeze rumors?
  A: No announced hiring freeze. We're monitoring spending and will share any changes early. For now, headcount plans continue in priority areas (runtime, SRE, product). If leadership decides otherwise we will communicate transparently.

Open items / questions for collaborators:
- Jordan: can you add up-to-date usage/metrics slides? (Need numbers by 2026-03-05)
- Priya: please draft the HR blurb about hiring / awards (2-3 sentences)
- Kai: verify the performance claims (25% tail latency reduction + batching benefit numbers). Add references to bench runs if available.
- Samira: customer quote + permission to use logo/metrics

Tone guide for speakers:
- Keep it short - 25-30 minutes total for meeting. Aim for clarity and celebration. Avoid deep product minutiae unless a direct ask.
- Use plain language for technical wins: translate impact to customer outcomes (cost, latency, reliability).

Rough run-of-show (timings):
- 0:00-0:03 CEO opening
- 0:03-0:11 Product update + demo (Emily/PM)
- 0:11-0:15 Eng wins + shout-outs
- 0:15-0:17 People ops updates
- 0:17-0:19 Customer highlight
- 0:19-0:30 Q&A (live)

Misc notes / scratch:
- Consider pre-submitting 3-4 questions to seed Q&A (execs often pull from these).
- Backup slide: short incident postmortem summary if asked (one-slide).
- Add link to all-hands recording + TL;DR email afterwards (action: Jordan).

Versioning: v0.1 - rough; will iterate.

(Fairly rough, lots of placeholders - meant as a working scratchpad; please edit directly.)
